overview: Black sets up the Gurgenidze structure with ...g6, ...d6, ...c6, ...Bg7 and ...Nf6 without ...Nf6 first, heading for ...Qb6 or ...b5 and ...Nbd7. White usually builds a centre with Be3, Qd2 and f3 or f4 and castles queenside for a kingside attack, or develops with Nf3 and Be2. Black has a solid structure but gives White space, and counterplay comes from ...b5 and ...e5.

white_ideas.idea: Build a big centre with Be3, f3 or f4, Qd2 and castle queenside
Attack with h4-h5 and Bh6 against the g7 bishop
Play Nf3, Be2 and O-O for a safe space advantage

black_ideas.idea: Use ...Qb6 or ...Qa5 to hit the centre and the queenside
Keep a solid structure and counterattack on the queenside

typical_structures.structure: White e4/d4 against Black c6/d6/g6 (Pirc-Modern type)
Austrian or 150 attack set-ups against a fianchetto bishop

character.notes: Black's compact c6/d6/g6 set-up is sound and hard to break, though White gets space.

structure.notes: White's centre against hypermodern pieces; tension is unresolved: flexible.

approach.notes: The Modern is a set-up Black can play against almost anything, so I lean to system, with low confidence.

level.notes: Plans are clear and there is not too much theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: Austrian-style 4.f4
sublines_that_differ.how: White goes for a big centre and the f4-f5 attack; Black has to react with ...Nf6 and ...Bg7.

character.reason: A compact structure that is hard to break down, though White gets space.

structure.reason: The centre is undecided and Black waits.

approach.reason: Black can use the set-up against almost anything.

plans.reason: Black lets White build a centre and attacks it with pieces and breaks.
